hero.sub: Anyone at {name} can make a launch post or image in seconds now. Without the brand's context, AI guesses: the wrong colors, the wrong voice and claims nobody approved.
hero.prompt: Make a LinkedIn post and image for our holiday campaign.
hero.generic: Excited to announce an amazing new feature! Our innovative AI solution will revolutionize the way your team works. Don't miss out! #Innovation #AI #Teamwork
hero.onbrand: This holiday, every Gap Inc. brand tells its own story from one shared plan. Find the approved campaign assets for Old Navy, Gap, Banana Republic and Athleta in one place.
hero.disclaimer: Illustrative draft written for this sample, using Gap Inc.'s public brand guidance. Not Gap Inc. content.
hero.headline: AI is making everyone a creative.
hero.headline2: That doesn't mean they're good at it.
hero.badCaption: Looks fine at a glance. Look again: the copy, the posed group, the colors.
hero.badAlt: A fictional AI-generated LinkedIn graphic: a posed fashion team, a royal blue wash and a generic headline

check.title: Then it checks the work
check.sub: Before anything goes live, Brand Check reviews it against {name}'s guidelines, flags potential issues, and shows which guideline informed each finding.
check.note: Brand Check runs on the context you already keep in Frontify. It's more than a prompt: it's a service built into Frontify, available in the portal and through the API. The image is fictional AI-generated work content, and the findings are samples.

asset.by: fictional, made with a generic AI image tool
asset.alt: A fictional AI-generated LinkedIn graphic: a posed fashion team, a royal blue wash and a generic headline

findings.text: The royal blue and gold overlay isn't the brand's navy.
findings.recommendation: Use navy, black and white for corporate work, with no color wash over photos.

findings.text: "Style Meets Innovation" is a generic line that doesn't sound like any of the four brands.
findings.recommendation: Write in the voice of the brand the post is for.

findings.text: A posed group smiling at the camera doesn't match the photography style.
findings.recommendation: Use a candid photo of a real team at work from the photo library.

items.label: Brand
items.title: Our palette
items.rule: Each brand keeps its own palette. Corporate work stays navy, black and white.
items.ask: Which color should a social post lead with?
items.answer: Use **Navy, #0F2441**. Each brand keeps its own palette.

items.label: Creative
items.title: Photography
items.lead: Real teams doing real work, never staged.

do.label: Teams at work
do.note: Candid moments of people working together.

dont.label: Posed for the camera
dont.note: No staged handshakes or stock smiles.

items.ask: Can I use a stock photo of a handshake?
items.answer: Better not. The photography guidelines ask for **candid teamwork**, and **no staged handshakes or stock smiles**.

items.desc: Short rules for email, decks and docs
items.title: Email tone of voice
items.lead: The short version of our tone of voice, for everyone who sends email.
rules: Say what you need in under eight words.
Lead with the ask or the answer.
Use the standard signature. No quotes or images.
items.do: Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?
items.dont: Just circling back on the below!!
items.askLabel: Before sending, in Outlook with Copilot
items.ask: Check this email against our writing guidelines.
items.answer: Two fixes before you send: **put the ask in the first line**, and **use the standard signature**.

everyday.eyebrow: Use case 4 · Everyday guidelines, inside your office applications
everyday.title: The right tone in every email and deck
everyday.sub: Most of {name} will never open a brand portal. With Frontify connected, Claude inside Outlook and PowerPoint reads the Everyday guidelines and checks the work before it goes out.
everyday.note: Claude for Microsoft 365 reads Frontify through the Frontify connector (MCP) once it's set up in your Claude workspace. Sample email, deck and guidelines.

tabs.label: Email in Outlook
tabs.ask: Check this email against our email tone of voice before I send it.
tabs.intro: Three fixes based on **Everyday › Email tone of voice**:

before.subject: Following up
body: Hi team, just circling back on the below!!
We've been heads-down on the holiday campaign and there's a lot going on, so I wanted to share where things stand.
Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?

after.subject: Review the holiday plan by Thursday
body: Hi team, can you review the holiday plan by Thursday?
It covers the messaging, launch assets and timeline. Comments in the doc are perfect.

fixes.label: Subject:
fixes.note: say what you need. "Following up" doesn't.

fixes.label: Opening:
fixes.note: lead with the ask. It's in the last line right now.

fixes.label: Sign-off:
fixes.note: use the standard signature, with no quotes.

tabs.done: Updated. The draft matches the email tone of voice and is ready to send.

fixes.label: Template:

fixes.label: Title:
fixes.note: 14 words. Keep titles to six or fewer.

fixes.label: Bullets:

partners.title: Agency files land in the right place
partners.sub: Agencies and licensees submit work straight into {name}'s portal. Files land in the right library, and the assistant tags them and sets an expiry date in one sentence.
partners.note: Sample files, agency and library. The assistant acts on the assets you select: workflow status, metadata, tags and expiry dates.
partners.ask: Tag these Holiday and Cleared for external use, and set them to expire Dec 31, 2026.
partners.plan: I'll add the tags Holiday and Cleared for external use, and set Available until to Dec 31, 2026, on the 2 selected assets. Say yes and I'll apply it.
partners.you: You're the agency. Then see what the brand team gets.

placements.label: Window
placements.where: Both windows, centered at eye level. Each brand dresses its own windows.
placements.content: Campaign art and the headline in that brand's look. Never mix two brands in one window.
placements.ask: Can the Old Navy and Gap windows share one graphic?
placements.answer: No. **Each brand dresses its own windows** in its own look. Pull each brand's window graphic from the campaign toolkit.

placements.label: Front table
placements.where: Front edge of the first table inside the door, facing the entrance.
placements.content: Headline and one line of copy. Folded stacks by size, smallest on top.
placements.ask: What goes on the front table this week?
placements.answer: The **Holiday gifts under $30** edit, with the **table header facing the entrance**. Fold stacks by size, smallest on top.

placements.label: Shelf
placements.where: Top of each wall fixture, at eye level.
placements.content: One product story per fixture, never two.
placements.ask: Can one shelf topper cover knits and denim?
placements.answer: **No. One product story per fixture.** Give denim its own topper on the next fixture.

placements.label: Register
placements.where: Left of the register, angled toward the customer.
placements.content: One add-on offer. Impulse items get price strips only.
placements.ask: What sign goes at the register this month?
placements.answer: One **counter card, left of the register**, angled toward the customer. For Holiday it is Add a gift card. Impulse items get **price strips only**.
